Dated this the 5th day of September, 2013
JUDGMENT
The petitioner seeks release of the goods detained under Ext.P4 notice.

Ext.P4 notice inter-alia states as follows:-
'As per the documents accompanied, the goods under transport is refined coconut oil - a non taxable item.
On physical verification, it is realised that the goods under transport is loosely consistent, odourless and colourless.

The goods actually transporting is  suspected to be inedible oil used for  other industrial purposes taxable at  5%'.
2.
The plea of stock transfer put-forth by the petitioner can be accepted only if the goods is established to be a coconut oil.
Whether the goods is a refined coconut oil as claimed can be deciphered only in the adjudication proceedings.

The Government Pleader points out that similar consignments have been released on Kaleesuwari Refinery Private Limited vs Intelligence Inspector on 29 August, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196287859/
3 orders of Court only after directing a portion of the security amount to be deposited.
3.

sentences.text: I direct the first respondent to release the goods so detained on condition that the petitioner deposits 25% of the sum demanded as security in Ext.P4 notice and executes a simple bond without surety for the balance sum.
The same shall however be subject to the adjudication proceedings which shall be finalised by the competent officer soon.
It is open to the petitioner in the enquiry to get a report from the Referal Food Laboratory or CSIR to test whether the goods transported is refined coconut oil or not.
The Writ Petition is disposed of.
V.CHITAMBARESH, JUDGE.
